text:
Zoe: FYI vuln-scan flagged decrypts from pod in ns `svc-ingest` using keystore socket owned by `svc-tenant`
Keenan: how are they reaching it? any hostPath or hostNetwork?
Zoe: evidence shows hostPath `/var/run/keystore.sock` mounted into a debug container on node pool `onprem-pool-3` and a privileged init container copied socket into podfs
Priya: oof. host-mounted keystore socket is a known risky pattern for onprem. quick mitigation: cordon node, evict pods from onprem-pool-3, remove hostPath mounts from deployments
Omar: adding network mitigations too: apply default deny egress in `svc-ingest` and only allow traffic to `keystore-proxy.svc.cluster.local:8443`
Nikhil: also verify CNI behavior — some CNIs expose host namespaces to pods if hostNetwork is used or hostport is misconfigured
Zoe: sample netpol I pushed to a test cluster: ```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress-to-keystore
  namespace: svc-ingest
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
    - to:
      - podSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: keystore-proxy
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 8443
```
Keenan: admission fix: create OPA/Gatekeeper constraint to deny Pod specs with hostPath that match `/var/run/keystore*` or with `hostNetwork: true` in tenant namespaces
Priya: temporary audit change: bump decrypt event retention for this customer to 180d and enable immediate alert for decrypts where `principal_namespace != key_namespace`
Omar: we should also tighten unix socket permissions on the host: set group to `keystore` and mode `0660`, run systemd unit to drop privileges for keystore-proxy so only its group can talk to socket
Nikhil: good call. on SELinux hosts add file context: `semanage fcontext -a -t keystore_var_run_t "/var/run/keystore.sock"` and restorecon, prevents unexpected processes from opening socket
Zoe: short checklist I'm doing: [1] cordon onprem-pool-3, [2] evict suspect pods, [3] revoke affected SA tokens, [4] rotate tenant keys, [5] apply netpol, [6] push gatekeeper constraint, [7] tighten host socket perms, [8] bump audit retention & alerting
Keenan: for RBAC audit, run: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]? | .name=="debug-runner")'` and search for any bindings that grant `system:masters`-like permissions to tenant SAs
Priya: customer comms: draft message ready. say: "we detected anomalous access path, applied containment, rotating keys, no evidence of exfil at this time, will share timeline after triage"
infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-ONPREM-KEYS by Priya; labels: ["onprem","kms","isolation"]
Omar: long-term: change agent design to avoid host socket if possible — use named in-cluster service with mTLS between keystore-proxy and agent, remove hostPath mounting entirely from the onprem package
Nikhil: also propose kubelet-level policy to disallow hostPath for tenant namespaces via NodeRestriction + admission controls
Zoe: updating incident doc with timeline and evidence. will paste logs here when I finish extraction
Keenan: I'll do RBAC sweep and post findings in ~45m
Priya: I'll coordinate customer update and SRE runbook steps. keep thread updated. thanks everyone.
